messages.subject: Covariate in multiple columns
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to make a covariate object by pulling genotype data from
multiple markers (or markers from single chromosome). Assigning a
single marker as covariate worked nicely. So I tried

> cov <- pull.geno(cross, chr=1)
> cov <- cross$geno[[1]]$data[,1:7]

but both gave this warning below and scanone generated nonspecific LOD
scores (all > 100).

1: In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar,
perm.strata, ... :
addcovar appears to be over-specified; consider dropping columns.

I know that pull.pheno(cross, c("sex", "age")) works beautifully,
which will generate 2 column object. So I manually made 2 column
object with random number and used it as covariate but still no luck.

Thanks!
Murim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Covariate in multiple columns
parts:
The problem is likely collinearity of the covariates in the linear
model that you are fitting. That is, the model is over-determined.
Consider the examples below.

I would suggest using only one or a few of the markers on the
chromosome as additive covariates.

karl
------

> data(fake.bc)
> fake.bc <- fill.geno(fake.bc)
> fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=1)
> out <- scanone(fake.bc)

> cov <- pull.geno(fake.bc, chr=1)
> out.a1 <- scanone(fake.bc, addcovar=cov)
> plot(out.a1)

[no problems]

> cov <- pull.geno(fake.bc, chr=c(1,2,5))
> out.a2 <- scanone(fake.bc, addcovar=cov)
> plot(out.a2)

[no problems]

> cov <- pull.geno(fake.bc, chr=c(5,13))
> out.a3 <- scanone(fake.bc, addcovar=cov)
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
> warnings()
Warning messages:

1: In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar,
perm.strata, ... :
addcovar appears to be over-specified; consider dropping columns.

2: X'X matrix is singular.
...

> plot(out.a3)

[LOD scores all > 300]
